status_summary: On 2026-07-13 the President signed Proclamation 11043, reducing Bears Ears National Monument from about 1.36 million to about 121,096 acres in two units and terminating the Bears Ears Commission, and Proclamation 11044, reducing Grand Staircase-Escalante from about 1.87 million to about 181,541 acres in two units (both published 2026-07-17). The excluded lands opened to entry, mineral and geothermal leasing and the mining laws at 9:00 a.m. Eastern time 60 days after signing (2026-09-11), subject to valid existing rights. On 2026-09-02 conservation-group plaintiffs represented by Earthjustice, NRDC and the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance moved in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (Hopi Tribe v. Trump, No. 1:17-cv-02590, ECF 269) to reopen the stayed 2017 case and add claims against Proclamation 11043; no ruling on the motion was found. A Federal Register listing of presidential documents mentioning national monuments since 2025-01-20 shows no proclamation for the Maine or Oregon monuments the Mandate named, and no proposal to repeal the Antiquities Act was found.

timeline.event: The President signs Proclamation 11043 modifying Bears Ears National Monument: reservation reduced from about 1.36 million acres to about 121,096 acres in two units; the Bears Ears Commission is terminated (published 2026-07-17).

The President signs Proclamation 11044 modifying Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument: reservation reduced from about 1.87 million acres to about 181,541 acres in two units (published 2026-07-17).

Conservation-group plaintiffs (counsel Earthjustice, NRDC and the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance) move in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (Hopi Tribe v. Trump, No. 1:17-cv-02590, ECF 269) to reopen the case, lift the stay in place since 2021 and file a second amended and supplemental complaint challenging Proclamation 11043.

title: Reduce national monuments, defend the reductions in court, and seek Antiquities Act repeal
uncertainties: The motion to reopen (ECF 269, filed 2026-09-02) was read on a copy hosted by the National Agricultural Law Center rather than on a court host; it challenges Proclamation 11043 and does not name Proclamation 11044, so whether and where the Grand Staircase-Escalante reduction is challenged was not confirmed. Reports differ on tribal participation: KUER said tribal nations were expected to file their own suits, and no tribal filing was read. The motion states that the Tenth Circuit decided Garfield County v. Trump on 2026-06-23; that decision was not read. The Federal Register listing of presidential documents mentioning national monuments since 2025-01-20 returned 18 items and only two modify monument boundaries; marine monument fishing proclamations (2025-04-22, 2026-02-11, 2026-06-17) change fishing rules and were not reviewed in full. No search was run for an Antiquities Act repeal bill beyond earlier limited searches.
